why: Prefix and suffix arrays: the product of everything except index i is (product of everything left of i) times (product of everything right of i). One left-to-right pass builds the prefix products, one right-to-left pass multiplies in the suffix products, with no division.
hints: Without division, split 'everything except i' into two parts you can precompute.
left[i] = product of nums[0..i-1], right[i] = product of nums[i+1..n-1]; answer[i] = left[i] * right[i].
Fill answer with prefix products in one pass, then sweep from the right with a running suffix product, multiplying it in. O(n) time, O(1) extra besides the output.
pitfalls: Zeros break the division trick, which is exactly why the task forbids it.
The first prefix and the last suffix are the empty product, 1.
